entries.acceptance: An affliction declares its resistance, onset and duration from its actual cause; health resistance is common but must not replace source-specific procedures.

An allowed drop can change standing to sitting, kneeling or prone, or kneeling/sitting to prone; it does not grant a normal maneuver.
An allowed stagger permits dropping, changing facing or moving/crawling one yard while still effectively stunned.

entries.acceptance: Choking prevents speech and breathing and permits only dropping; use suffocation. A lodged object can be cleared by a two-second first-aid attempt, at -2 before technology seven.
No-breathing or homogeneous anatomy prevents choking; assess immunity before creating a suffocation episode.
A dazed actor can remain standing but cannot act; being struck, slapped or shaken permits recovery on the next turn, not an immediate extra action.
Use agony-like incapacity without pain-tolerance modifiers, and replace the threatened-pain bonus with +3 influence for offering continued pleasure; inability to enjoy pleasure grants immunity.
Before each attempted success roll while hallucinating, make the required will check; success produces two dice of seconds of disorientation at -2, failure one die of minutes at -5.
Critical will failure causes three dice of minutes of uncontrolled behavior, with an authored reaction informed by a three-dice danger roll; retain nonvisual hallucination possibilities.
Paralysis prevents voluntary muscle movement and causes a fall if unbalanced, but preserves consciousness and abilities requiring neither speech nor movement.
entries.validation_note: Owned finite conscious paralysis now applies balanced-position onset, voluntary movement/speech restrictions, Do Nothing handling and explicit mental-ability permission through the shared action gate. Permission fields are receipt-bound. Physical medical care now consults movement availability; bandaging boundary assertions specify no time, healing or randomness while paralyzed and normal care after expiry. Fixtures authored, unrun. Poison causes, height falls and individual power/defense adapters remain incomplete.

entries.acceptance: Strong-acid splash inflicts one die minus three corrosion damage; a face splash also requires a health check for eye exposure.
A failed face-exposure health check or a direct eye hit routes damage to eyes and uses crippling rules; a critical exposure failure guarantees permanent blindness.
Immersion inflicts one die minus one corrosion damage each second, with a fresh eye-exposure check each second the face is immersed.
Swallowed acid creates a three-dice injury total delivered one point each fifteen minutes; successful physician or poison treatment taking two dice of minutes halts remaining injury.
Acid can dissolve a lock's pins or similar small vulnerable item in three dice of minutes; bind the effect to the target and actual reagent.
A vial with the listed strength is available from technology three and costs ten currency units; strong alkalis use the same hazard model.
Scale atmospheric pressure bands by native pressure; composition and pressure are independent hazards, so a breathable pressure is insufficient to establish safe air.
Thin air adds one fatigue to exertion costs and -1 vision without eye protection.

After at least an hour breathing thin air, make a daily health+4 altitude check: ordinary success has no effect, critical success acclimatizes, failure imposes -2 dexterity/intelligence and critical failure causes coma after one die of hours.
A physician may attempt a daily revival check for altitude coma; preserve the actual onset and death/recovery state.
Dense breathable air imposes -1 to all health checks without a pressure suit; high oxygen additionally requires a reducing respirator or causes -2 dexterity.
Author gas composition, concentration, exposure route, equipment coverage and physiological compatibility; support concurrent corrosive, toxic and suffocating components.
For a small corrosive concentration in breathable air, check health with authored modifier zero through -4 each minute; failure inflicts one corrosion damage.
Corrosive-atmosphere injury reaching one-third capacity causes coughing and two-thirds causes blindness; track injury from this exposure instead of substituting all preexisting injury.
A predominantly corrosive atmosphere uses acid-immersion effects and also suffocates; sealing protects only while its material remains intact against the gas.
Ordinary airborne pollution may require a daily health check to avoid one toxic damage; specify the actual pollutant and exposure.
Lethal low-concentration gases require an authored health penalty from -2 through -6 each minute to avoid one toxic damage.
A predominantly toxic atmosphere inflicts at least one die toxic damage per fifteen seconds without resistance and also suffocates.
Apply actual respirator, no-breathing or filtered-lung protection to the appropriate gas hazard; skin or eye exposure can remain despite protected breathing.
An atmosphere lacking the actor's required breathing component causes suffocation unless an independent air supply or no-breathing trait protects them.
Up to 0.01 times native pressure uses vacuum rules.
Above trace through 0.5 times native pressure is unbreathable without protection and imposes -2 vision without eye protection.
The printed thin band is 0.51 through 0.8 times native pressure; apply thin-air exertion, vision and altitude effects.
The printed normal band is 0.81 through 1.2 times native pressure.
The printed dense band is 1.21 through 1.5 times native pressure; reducing respiration is needed when oxygen exceeds fifty percent.
The printed very-dense band begins at 1.51 times native pressure and needs reducing respiration when oxygen exceeds ten percent.
At ten or more times native pressure, apply very-dense effects and the pressure-injury rules separately.
Define how supplied hundredth-atmosphere bands classify more precise boundary values without silently inventing gaps; record the chosen supported measurement precision.
Below the actor's cold comfort threshold, roll the better of health and health-based arctic survival every thirty minutes, shortened by wind.

Occupants in a sudden stop take fall-equivalent damage from lost speed; restraints give resistance five and airbags ten.

entries.acceptance: A named electrical attack's own procedure overrides generic electrical guidance; distinguish lethal, nonlethal and localized current.
Metallic armor gives only one resistance against electricity; a grounded wearer attracts attacks for +2 attacker accuracy.
A nonlethal shock calls for immediate health resistance with authored intensity, modified by nonmetallic armor resistance and the attack's armor divisor.
A surface shock uses armor divisor one-half, while an arc weapon can use two or five as defined; do not apply the divisor twice when deriving resistance bonus.
An instantaneous nonlethal jolt that defeats resistance stuns for one second, then permits health recovery each second.
A continuous shock holds stun through contact and for max(one, twenty minus health) seconds afterward, then permits per-second recovery.
Electrical recovery checks retain the intensity modifier but omit the armor-resistance bonus from the initial check.
A muscle-disrupting shock uses health-5 and causes knockdown/paralysis instead of ordinary stun, preserving the same contact and recovery timing.
Lethal electricity inflicts burning damage with the authored strength, ranging from small household shocks to six dice or more for powerful sources.
After any whole-body electrical injury, check health at -1 per two injury; failure causes unconsciousness through contact and max(one, twenty minus health) minutes afterward.
After electrical unconsciousness, apply -2 dexterity for the listed twenty-minus-health-minute interval; resolve nonpositive boundary handling explicitly from applicable rules.
Whole-body electrical resistance failure by five or more, or critical failure, causes cardiac arrest through the health condition procedure.
Lethal electricity also triggers surge rules for electrically vulnerable actors, including machines.

Localized electrical injury uses burning damage and the injury-based health penalty, but failure causes one-second stun followed by recovery instead of automatic whole-body unconsciousness or cardiac arrest.
Localized electrical injury to a hand or arm also requires a will check to retain held objects in that hand.
Partial-turn fire exposure causes one die minus three burning damage through the large-area injury procedure.
A full turn in ordinary fire or being fully aflame causes one die minus one burning damage per second; intense fire such as a furnace can cause three dice per second.
An incendiary attack adds a linked one-point burning component to its other damage; retain separate armor and ignition handling as specified.
A single burning roll meeting the material threshold ignites it; divide tight-beam burning by ten for ignition purposes.
If the source could ignite the material on its best roll, roll its damage once per second of contact until ignition or separation.
If the source cannot reach the threshold, check three dice per ten contact seconds: a material one class harder ignites on sixteen or less, two classes harder on six or less.
A burning material can ignite adjacent materials; each target needs its own exposure history and rolls based on the actual source fire damage.
A single hit of at least three basic burning damage ignites part of ordinary clothing, causing one die minus four per second and -2 dexterity unless harmless to the wearer.
Beating out partial clothing fire uses a dexterity roll and one ready maneuver per attempt.
A hit of at least ten basic burning damage ignites all ordinary clothing, causing one die minus one per second and -3 dexterity except on extinguishing checks.
Rolling out full clothing fire uses a dexterity roll and three ready maneuvers per attempt; entering water extinguishes automatically in one second.
A wooden shield taking at least ten burning damage in one second gives its bearer -2 dexterity and one die minus five burning damage per second until discarded.
Apply shock from actual fire injury alongside any separate burning distraction penalty, without applying either twice.
Armor still reduces damage from overlying burning clothing; wet or covered clothing is very difficult to ignite and does not sustain flame under the stated conditions.
An authored readily ignitable garment can ignite at one burning damage; retain the tight-beam reduction and the actual clothing construction.
The most flammable class can ignite from negligible candle-like heat.
Highly flammable material ignites at one burning damage.
Ordinary flammable material ignites at three burning damage.
Resistant material ignites at ten burning damage.
Highly resistant material ignites at thirty burning damage.
Nonflammable material does not ignite through the ordinary burning threshold procedure.
On first entering microgravity/free fall, a nonnative actor checks the higher of health or free-fall skill, with -4 from the relevant sickness trait.
Failed entry checking causes nausea; retching in a sealed suit can choke the actor and uses the drowning procedure.
Retry the better health/free-fall check every eight hours to adapt, except that an actor with the sickness disadvantage cannot adapt.
Sudden acceleration at least 2.5 times home gravity requires health checking, treating home gravity below 0.1G as 0.1G for this trigger.
Apply -2 per doubling of acceleration, with the printed five-times-home and ten-times-home examples at -2 and -4; seated/prone gives +2 and upside down -2.
Failed acceleration resistance loses fatigue equal to failure margin; critical failure also blacks out for ten seconds times that margin.
Being thrown against a solid surface by acceleration uses collision velocity ten times the acceleration in gravities; distinguish collision injury from resistance-check fatigue.
Underwater pressure rises approximately one atmosphere per thirty-three feet; apply native pressure and actual protective traits.
Above ten times native pressure check health at entry and every minute, using +3 minus one per ten-times-native increment; failure injury equals margin, multiplied by size modifier if at least +2.

entries.acceptance: Safe decompression needs an authored sequence based on pressure and exposure time, potentially hours or days; the example safe limits do not supply a complete interpolation table.
entries.validation_note: Explicit approved descending schedules now execute as owned pressure stages with shared-clock progress receipts, deadline integration, bound definitions and checked progress history. No duration is interpolated. Concurrent schedules, abandonment/emergency ascent, changing protection and illness remain unsupported. Lifecycle fixtures authored, unrun.

entries.acceptance: Unsafe decompression requires health checking: critical success has no effect, success causes agony with hourly health recovery, failure causes unconsciousness or painful paralysis and critical failure causes death.
After ordinary decompression failure, hourly health failure causes one die injury; successful awakening transitions to the ongoing joint-pain recovery phase.
Recompression to the highest experienced pressure allows health+4 checks every five minutes to recover effects short of death.
Instant pressure loss can also cause explosive-decompression effects; record all applicable consequences without substituting one for the other.

On the first day aboard a qualifying vessel, apply the motion-sickness trait procedure; without that trait use health+5, with success by five or critical success avoiding all effects. Stabilized large modern vessels are exempt.
Complete lack of air spends one fatigue per second after any permitted breath reserve; at zero fatigue check will each second to remain conscious.
entries.validation_note: Owned no-reserve airless seconds and rescue authored. Expected-value, transaction, undo, save continuation and breath-ownership fixtures remain unrun. Breath-reserve handoff, exceptional physiology, drowning and broad cross-module verification remain incomplete.

entries.acceptance: Drowning with partial air access uses swimming checks every five seconds and fatigue on failure instead of also imposing complete-airlessness costs.
Four minutes without air kills regardless of current health or fatigue, unless an applicable physiological trait changes the procedure.
entries.validation_note: Owned no-reserve airless seconds, shared air ledger, fatigue/overflow, consciousness and clean-air rescue authored. Fixtures unrun. Breath-reserve handoff, exceptional physiology, drowning, full transaction/persistence and cross-module verification remain incomplete.

entries.acceptance: Clean air before death ends suffocation costs and enables ordinary fatigue recovery; unconsciousness from this cause ends at positive fatigue.

entries.acceptance: A drowning rescue also requires the specified first-aid/resuscitation success to clear water; access to clean air alone is insufficient.
More than two minutes without air requires a health check to avoid permanent intelligence loss of one; apply it once for the exposure and recalculate dependent scores.

entries.acceptance: Vacuum and trace-atmosphere exposure require appropriate suit or vacuum-support protection, while independent oxygen needs remain separately assessed.
Holding breath in vacuum risks one die injury from lung rupture; exhaling permits half ordinary breath-holding duration from blood oxygen before suffocation begins.
Sudden normal-to-near-zero pressure loss causes one die immediate injury and a health check for decompression illness.
Explosive decompression checks each eye separately at health+2 and hearing at health-1; failed checks impose the corresponding sensory loss with crippling-duration resolution.
Vacuum has no intrinsic hot/cold damage value; use authored radiant exposure and surface temperatures, with their actual thermal contact.
At up to two atmospheres, a baseline human can return without slow decompression after any duration.
